verdicts.claim: A checkpoint transfers WAL changes into the main database
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file."

verdicts.claim: ordinary checkpointing need not reduce the WAL file's physical size because SQLite can reuse its allocated space
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file ... it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning."

verdicts.claim: SQLite's default automatic checkpoint threshold is 1000 pages
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages." Litestream doc agrees.

verdicts.claim: the 1000-page threshold is configurable at build time or runtime
verdicts.evidence: wal.html cites SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option and wal_autocheckpoint pragma / sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint().
wal.html: "All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE."

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE copies as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and never invokes the busy handler; may be incomplete
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting ... The busy-handler callback is never invoked ... might leave the checkpoint unfinished."

verdicts.claim: A successful TRUNCATE checkpoint adds zero-length WAL truncation to RESTART behavior
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return."

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) exposes this operation in SQL
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "The PRAGMA wal_checkpoint command can be used to invoke this interface from SQL."; Turso blog shows the TRUNCATE pragma as "Checkpoint and truncate the WAL file".

verdicts.claim: Long-running reader snapshots can prevent checkpoint progress or WAL reset; overlapping readers permit continued WAL growth
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "if ... there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound."

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: Litestream says FULL blocks new readers and PASSIVE fails when readers exist; SQLite API allows new readers during FULL
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: FULL "Blocks new readers", PASSIVE "Fails if readers present"; c3ref FULL: "new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded."
